name: diagnosis
title: Ambiguous diagnosis (why is biomass low?)
question: A cell's biomass is far below target. Diagnose the cause from the observables and add the mechanism that fixes it, so the cell both grows (biomass >= 3.0) and stays alive (viability >= 0.5).
biological_summary: A process-bigraph Composite: CellGrowth (Monod uptake → yield growth, GATED by viability) + MembraneStress (viability decay). Biomass is low because the cell is DYING, not because of yield or uptake — a cause diagnosable only from the joint observables (nutrient fully consumed, viability crashed). The fix is stabilize_membrane.
conclusion:
## Final model
A process-bigraph Composite: CellGrowth (Monod uptake → yield growth, GATED by viability) + MembraneStress (viability decay). Biomass is low because the cell is DYING, not because of yield or uptake — a cause diagnosable only from the joint observables (nutrient fully consumed, viability crashed). The fix is stabilize_membrane.

## Result
DONE (2/2) in 1 edit — the LLM read the joint observable panel (nutrient fully consumed → uptake fine; viability crashed → cell dying) and installed the one correct fix. The deterministic policy MISDIAGNOSED: it hill-climbed the worst margin, installed boost_yield, growth still failed, and it gave up — a low-growth margin alone cannot name the cause. See docs/diagnosis-agent-vs-policy.html.

findings.statement: Low biomass was caused by the cell DYING, not by a broken yield or uptake pathway — a cause diagnosable only from the joint observables (nutrient fully consumed, so uptake is fine; viability crashed, so the cell is dying). Adding the correct mechanism, stabilize_membrane against the MembraneStress viability decay, restores growth so biomass reaches its target (biomass >= 3.0).
